services.name: Measure Edge Delivery page and block interactions
owner: Edge Delivery Services + Customer Journey Analytics
services.scope: Instrument the agreed page and block events on Edge Delivery that the existing collection does not capture. Use the existing consent controls, Web SDK, datastream, dataset and CJA connection. Verify consent handling and trace sample events to the CJA data view. Assign consent platform integration and any shared collection setup once under the site or analytics work.
services.adobe_quote: This quick start guide explains how you can ingest website tracking data directly into Adobe Experience Platform using the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK and Edge Network and then use that data in Customer Journey Analytics.

source.title: Experience League: Ingest data via the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK

connection_how: Edge-delivered pages send consented website events through Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK. Customer Journey Analytics reads the event dataset through a configured CJA connection and data view.
product_facts: Edge Delivery Services is Adobe's content delivery framework, a core part of Adobe Experience Manager, built for speed, simplicity and scalability. It works with your own CDN or the included Adobe-managed CDN.
Edge Delivery Services delivers the site's pages, built for speed.
We would build the site on Edge Delivery Services with its code managed and deployed directly from a GitHub repository. New content is added instantly, without a rebuild process.

Every project on Edge Delivery Services should produce a Lighthouse score of 100 for mobile and desktop, measured with Google PageSpeed Insights. Adobe's guidance is that the score is not hard to keep at 100 with continuous testing, so we would test each change.

Your authors can work in AEM Authoring, which includes Document Authoring and AEM Sites Author, or in Microsoft SharePoint or Google Drive. They get an instant URL to see their content changes and share them with others for review.

For your existing site, Adobe's importer automates importing and converting multiple pages. We would make example imports of each page type so your authors can confirm the structure, and reflect retired URLs in the redirects spreadsheet.
Customer Journey Analytics brings Analysis Workspace to the data in Adobe Experience Platform, so journeys can be analyzed across channels in one reporting view.
Customer Journey Analytics measures the results across channels.

In Customer Journey Analytics your data can be viewed and analyzed in sequence across channels: data from your call center, point-of-sale systems and online properties is combined into a single reporting view.

Results are measured in Customer Journey Analytics, used as the reporting source for Target's A/B activities: its Experimentation panel compares the variations and reports each one's lift over the baseline, and the confidence in it, on the success metrics you choose.
All data that is ingested into Adobe Experience Platform must conform to a pre-defined schema before it can be persisted as a dataset.
Set up a datastream to configure the Adobe Experience Platform Edge Network to route your collected data to the dataset you configured in Adobe Experience Platform.
Set up a connection in Customer Journey Analytics. This connection should (at least) include your Adobe Experience Platform dataset.

A data view is a container specific to Customer Journey Analytics that lets you determine how to interpret data from a connection. It specifies all dimensions and metrics available in Analysis Workspace and which columns those dimensions and metrics obtain their data from.
The setConsent command tells the Web SDK if it should send data (opt in), discard data (opt out), or use defaultConsent (consent unknown).

services.name: Brand validation results in Frame.io review
services.scope: Agree with your client's review leads at which step of their Frame.io reviews the brand validation results are read and what happens to an asset that fails before sign-off, then try the agreed steps on one real review.
services.adobe_quote: Apply brand checks as assets move through review workflows, instead of running validation as a separate manual step.

source.title: Adobe for Business: Brand validation with Adobe Brand Intelligence

connection_how: We agree with your review leads where in your Frame.io reviews the brand validation results from Adobe Brand Intelligence are read and what happens to an asset that fails, then try it on a real review.
product_facts: Frame.io is where your creative teams and their stakeholders organize, review and manage creative assets as they move from ideation to final approval.
Frame.io is where creative assets are organized, reviewed and managed on their way to final approval.

Reviewers and approvers add comments, mark up the asset and make the approval decision in the Frame.io viewer, which provides version history and comparison and time-stamped comments for video reviews.

Each user has an account role, assigned in the Adobe Admin Console, that sets their baseline permissions: Content Admins have administrative access to all public resources, and Members need an explicit invitation to reach a project or workspace.
Frame.io has a REST API and webhooks for custom workflows and automations, and server-to-server authentication integrates it with your other tools without relying on individual user accounts.

Brand Intelligence is a continuously learning platform that helps your teams create and validate on-brand content. It learns from your assets, past reviews and team decisions, and is a headless platform exposed through APIs rather than a separate app.

The Validate skill automatically checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live, across designs, images, documents and layouts. Each approval, edit or rejection of a suggestion feeds back into Brand Intelligence for continuous learning.

Native integrations. Surface validation results directly within connected tools such as Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Workfront, and Frame.io for Business, so teams can review content where they already work.
You can easily integrate it into apps such as Workfront and Frame.

Use Validate to quickly check whether your content is compliant with your organization’s brand identity and guidelines. Catch issues early, fix them faster, and move assets through review efficiently.

services.name: Brand checks on production workflow outputs
services.scope: Agree with your client's production lead which production workflows have their outputs validated against brand guidelines, estimate the Operations the checks use at the planned volume, run a test batch through to the results in Frame.io, and agree which failed outputs are rerun before review.
services.adobe_quote: Automatically validate production outputs against brand guidelines and display results in Frame.io for review and sign-off.

source.title: Adobe for Business: Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise

connection_how: We agree with you which of your production workflows have their outputs validated against your brand guidelines, and we test that the results reach your reviewers in Frame.io.
product_facts: Firefly Creative Production is Adobe's enterprise offering for scaled content automation. It brings together workflow authoring, headless creative services and a production runtime to produce on-brand outputs at scale, for work such as campaign variants, localization and templated asset production.
Firefly Creative Production produces on-brand outputs at scale through reusable workflows.

We would turn your existing production playbook into reusable workflows: define the inputs, assemble the steps, add logic and test the flow, then link it to your source systems, review tools and storage locations so that it fits into your existing environment.

The Workflow API executes published workflows across multiple assets in one batch. Your external platforms can trigger workflow executions, with processed outputs returned to the originating environment, and Firefly Services APIs cover headless and programmatic use cases.

Your admin assigns access in the Admin Console. Workflow authoring and admin access can stay with a smaller group of specialists, while a broader group runs the published workflows, guided experiences, APIs or bulk actions.

Teams monitor progress and review results on each run, focusing attention on exceptions rather than on every asset. The Workflow API returns batch status with asset counts, execution statistics and estimated time remaining.

Brand Intelligence is a continuously learning platform that helps your teams create and validate on-brand content. It learns from your assets, past reviews and team decisions, and is a headless platform exposed through APIs rather than a separate app.

The Validate skill automatically checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live, across designs, images, documents and layouts. Each approval, edit or rejection of a suggestion feeds back into Brand Intelligence for continuous learning.
Operations are licensed through Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise offering or the Shared Credits offering.
Use of Skills consumes Operations as set forth in the Rate Card.
The consumption rate of Operations for each Skill is set forth in the Rate Card.

services.name: Instruct to Assemble rollout for designers in Figma
services.scope: Train your client's designers to run the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin in Figma: choose the context, set the number of variants, review what it assembles, adjust single assets or regenerate with other assembly options, and agree how finished variants go on to review.
services.adobe_quote: You can make manual adjustments to individual assets if needed, or regenerate variants with different assembly options.

source.title: Adobe Firefly help: Instruct to Assemble

connection_how: Your team uses the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin in Figma to create on-brand variants from your predefined templates, with images selected, cropped and checked against your brand guidelines automatically.
product_facts: Brand Intelligence is a continuously learning platform that helps your teams create and validate on-brand content. It learns from your assets, past reviews and team decisions, and is a headless platform exposed through APIs rather than a separate app.
Brand Intelligence checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live.

Brand Intelligence brings together your brand guidelines, design systems, creative assets, human feedback and approvals, and your brand profile is configured during onboarding. Because it is a headless platform exposed through APIs, we would then integrate it with your existing apps.

The Validate skill automatically checks whether content adheres to your brand standards before it goes live, across designs, images, documents and layouts. Each approval, edit or rejection of a suggestion feeds back into Brand Intelligence for continuous learning.
The Instruct to Assemble skill turns a campaign brief into on-brand content variants by selecting the best-fit creative elements and assembling them into production-ready outputs.

It integrates through APIs: your systems submit a batch of assets and receive structured pass/fail feedback per asset, authenticated with OAuth Server-to-Server credentials set up in the Adobe Developer Console.
You can use Instruct to assemble in Figma via the Adobe Brand Intelligence plugin to quickly create multiple on-brand variants using predefined templates and brand guidelines.
Select the appropriate Context from the dropdown menu that matches your campaign or brand requirements, such as channel, audience, and product data.
Under the Variant preference, enter the Number of variants you want to create for each design.
Start with 2-3 variants when testing a new context configuration to verify output quality before generating larger batches.
Review the assembled results to confirm they meet your campaign requirements.
You can easily integrate it into apps such as Figma.
These options are custom to your brand and campaign identity and are configured in the Adobe Brand Artifactory.

services.name: Coworker set up in an AI platform
services.scope: Help the Client's administrators approve and deploy Coworker in one AI platform the Client already uses that Adobe supports for Coworker: Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini Enterprise or Databricks Genie One. Test the agreed example prompts with the pilot users under their own Adobe permissions, and show the team what Coworker answers there.
services.adobe_quote: Your administrator must approve Coworker before you add it.

source.title: Experience League: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker for AI Platforms

services.template_deliverable: Coworker approved and deployed for the pilot users in the agreed platform, a tested prompt set and a short guide to what Coworker answers there and what stays in the Coworker interface.
services.template_acceptance: Pilot users open Coworker in the agreed platform and get answers that match the data they can see in their Adobe applications.
services.template_assumptions: Coworker is provisioned for the Client's organization and each pilot user has access to it in Adobe. The Client has Adobe Experience Platform and at least one of Real-Time CDP, Journey Optimizer or Customer Journey Analytics, and access to the AI platform. The Client's administrators for that platform approve and deploy Coworker; for Databricks Genie One they also have the Client ID and secret for the Coworker MCP service and permission to install an MCP service in the chosen Unity Catalog catalog and schema. There, Coworker returns read-only insights within each user's Adobe permissions, does not offer every Coworker capability and draws on the same AI credits as other Coworker work. Pilot users are a training scope, not a seat limit.
services.template_exclusions: AI platform licenses, platforms or custom agent harnesses Adobe does not support for Coworker, actions that change data, new Skills or connections, and training already covered by another selected service.
services.template_basis: One AI platform, up to 10 pilot users and five test prompts. Adobe charges nothing extra for Coworker in AI platforms: it is part of the Coworker license and draws on the same AI credits.
product_facts: Coworker is Adobe's AI-powered teammate for customer experience and marketing workflows. You describe a goal in plain language, and it plans the work, executes it across your Adobe and connected systems, validates the results and brings the finished work back for your approval.
Coworker lets your teams ask for insights, content and actions across your Adobe applications in natural language.

We would tailor Coworker to the way your teams work with skills: reusable playbooks that standardize common workflows, reporting methods and analysis approaches, so nobody has to explain the same process again.

You keep control through approval gates, permissions inherited from your Adobe organization, checks before actions run and an audit trail. Skills do not store customer data: data access stays governed through your connected Adobe applications, permissions and organizational controls.
Coworker acts across Adobe and external systems through governed access, using built-in connectors or your own. An external tool or service is connected by adding it as a server.
As Coworker takes on a task you can watch it reason and progress. It validates the results and brings the finished work back to you for approval.
Use Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker for AI Platforms to get marketing insights in the AI tools you already use.
Coworker inherits those permissions, so no separate permissions setup is required for the AI platform integration.
Coworker returns read-only insights and does not modify your customer data.
Review any generated summaries and analyses before you use them to make business decisions.
Coworker in AI platforms does not support all capabilities available in the Coworker interface.
Each user signs in with their Adobe account. Coworker requests use that user’s Adobe permissions.
Find available platforms and their setup instructions in Set up Coworker.

services.name: Workfront Fusion scenarios with Coworker
services.scope: Connect Coworker to Workfront Fusion with an account your client chooses, since Coworker can change whatever that account can and the modules cannot limit individual tools. Build and test the agreed scenario around Run a Prompt and Get Execution Status: its trigger, a prompt mapped from earlier modules, storage and follow-on modules, results that need input or approval routed to a person, Task IDs saved for long tasks, a check that each completed run did its business action, and error handling that never resends a prompt whose outcome is uncertain.
services.adobe_quote: The connector starts and checks Coworker requests. It does not monitor project changes or automatically save answers to another application. Add the appropriate trigger, storage, and follow-on modules to your scenario as needed.
services.license: Workfront Fusion (part of Workfront Ultimate and of Workflow plus Automation and Integration packages; Prime and Select without Automation and Integration need it bought separately)

source.title: Experience League: Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker modules (Workfront Fusion)

connection_how: Workfront Fusion’s Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker connector sends a natural-language prompt to Coworker and uses its response in a scenario: Run a Prompt starts a new request, and Get Execution Status checks a request started earlier.
product_facts: Workfront is Adobe's suite of cloud-based applications for planning, project management, collaboration and resource management. It organizes, prioritizes, tracks and manages both your work and your resources.
Workfront organizes, prioritizes, tracks and manages the work and its resources.

We would set up request queues, so every request is submitted the same way and follows the same path to completion, with routing rules that send each one to a user, job role, team or project, and project templates that capture your repeatable processes.
Reviews and approvals can be one-time or come from reusable approval templates, with multi-stage approvals and parallel paths, and comprehensive audit logging keeps a complete governance trail.
Workfront organizes information in reports, places multiple reports on a dashboard and lets you share both reports and dashboards with others.
Access is governed at two levels: your Workfront administrator sets the access levels, and within those levels people share objects with view, contribute or manage permissions.
Run a Prompt starts a new request and, by default, waits for the result.
Get Execution Status checks a request that you started earlier.
Select whether you are connecting to a service account or a personal account.
Coworker can use tools and perform actions allowed by your account, including changes to records. Use trusted prompts and an account with appropriate access.
These modules do not provide a way to restrict individual tools.
Route the result to a person instead of treating it as completed work.
For longer work, turn waiting off and save the initial Task ID so you can check the task later.
Completed does not guarantee that the requested business action succeeded.
Make sure your scenario’s error handling does not repeat a prompt whose outcome is uncertain.
